claims.quote: With nine compartments flooded the ship would still float
claims.description: A giant liner with nine flooded watertight compartments would still stay afloat, so it is considered practically unsinkable.

claims.quote: These doors would also close automatically in the presence of water.
claims.description: Watertight compartment doors that close automatically when water is detected.

claims.quote: each wire terminating in a marked dial with a movable indicator
claims.description: Hidden telegraph wires carry the bridge's orders to indicator dials at every work station on the ship.

claims.quote: She was eight hundred feet long, of seventy thousand tons' displacement, seventy-five thousand horse-power
claims.description: A steamship about 800 feet long, displacing 70,000 tons, with 75,000 horsepower.

claims.quote: she would steam at full speed in fog, storm, and sunshine
claims.description: A company rule keeps the liner at full speed in all weather, on the theory that a fast ship suffers less collision damage.

claims.quote: would land her passengers three thousand miles away with the promptitude and regularity of a railway train
claims.description: A transatlantic liner keeps a fixed schedule as regular as a railway train.

claims.quote: while at full speed, she would cut her in two with no more damage to herself than a paintbrush could remedy
claims.description: A giant liner at full speed would cut a smaller ship in two while suffering almost no damage itself.

claims.quote: at the most three compartments would be flooded
claims.description: A head-on collision with an iceberg would flood at most three compartments, which the ship could survive.

claims.quote: had enabled her designers to discard the flat, kettle-bottom of cargo boats
claims.description: Because the ship carries no cargo, her hull is built with a deep V-shaped bottom like a steam yacht for better performance in heavy seas.
